transcript:
Header: 2026-10-06 14:00 UTC | Duration: ~60 mins
Attendees: Jordan Blake (Redwood AE), Priya Nair (Redwood SE), Samir Patel (Redwood ML), Olivia Chen (Redwood SE), Emma Liu (SageHealth ML Lead), Carlos Ramirez (SageHealth Platform), Maya Singh (SageHealth Security), Tom Becker (SageHealth Product)

Summary: Weekly POC sync to review INT8 vs FP8 quantization experiments. Covered perf deltas, quality regressions on evaluation set, memory/throughput tradeoffs, and next steps for a canary on Dedicated.

00:00:00 Jordan: All right, hey everyone, thanks for joining, uh we'll kick off. Agenda is quick review of last week's experiments, results from the larger eval run, and then next steps for canary.
00:00:18 Emma: Sounds good; sorry I'm running a little late, jumping in now.
00:00:24 Priya: No worries. Quick note, some of the numbers in the sheet were adjusted after the tokenizer mapping bug, Samir fixed that yesterday so the deltas we discuss are post-fix.
00:00:40 Carlos: Good to know. Can you call out which model variants you used? We want to map to our infra.
00:00:48 Priya: Sure — baseline was FP16 baseline Redwood-13B-v1. Then we ran INT8 dynamic and the FP8 hybrid profile (aarch/FP8-lite) with the same seq len distribution you gave us. For the INT8 we used the per-channel calibration with MSE + KL combined, and for FP8 we used the alpha scaling from the RPQ paper — hairier details in the notes.
00:01:08 Tom: When you say "INT8 dynamic" is that post-training quant or quant-aware training?
00:01:13 Samir: It's post-training quantization with small calibration set (2k samples) — no QAT yet. We flagged QAT as a follow-up if the regressed prompts are critical.
00:01:26 Maya: From a security perspective we also need a note on determinism for reproducible audits — do quant modes change op ordering?
00:01:34 Olivia: They shouldn't change logical op ordering; there is kernel selection variance but that's not surfaced in logs beyond latency/perf. We'll add a short note for your compliance team.

00:02:05 Priya: OK onto numbers — representative eval (5k prompts, mixed instructions + completion style). Latency p50 for FP16 baseline was 210ms. INT8 p50 170ms (-19%), FP8 p50 150ms (-29%). p95 for FP16 was 620ms, INT8 520ms (-16%), FP8 460ms (-26%).
00:02:35 Emma: Those p95 drops look great. What about throughput and GPU mem?
00:02:41 Samir: Memory footprint: FP16 ~22GB, INT8 ~14.5GB (-34%), FP8 ~12.8GB (-42%). Throughput (tokens/sec) on our Dedicated test node: FP16 420 tok/s, INT8 610 tok/s (+45%), FP8 690 tok/s (+64%).
00:03:02 Carlos: Nice — that memory saving might let us double burst capacity on our planned Dedicated pool. Any accuracy regressions?
00:03:10 Priya: This is the meat of it. Overall Rouge/rouge-like and BLEU-ish signal shows small drops: INT8 mean metric delta -0.7% relative, FP8 -1.9% relative. But token-level quality varies by prompt type: instruction-heavy prompts showed tiny deltas, long-form summarization saw more regressions with FP8.
00:03:34 Emma: Can you show examples?
00:03:38 Priya: Yep. We have a "regressions" sheet in the spreadsheet — quick excerpt: Prompt A (clinical note summarization) baseline: "Patient denies chest pain..."; INT8 kept fidelity, FP8 occasionally dropped negation word "denies" in 3/100 samples — that's unacceptable for some safety-critical flows.
00:03:59 Emma: That's concerning. Which tokens were getting clipped?
00:04:04 Samir: Seems related to logits compression in certain head outputs for longer contexts; rare but correlated with low-frequency tokens and with our model's tokenizer join rules. We think a targeted per-layer clipping or mixed-precision on attention softmax could fix it.
00:04:21 Olivia: Also, the FP8 hybrid profile we used applies aggressive compression to feed-forward layers — we can try preserving FFN in FP16 while quantizing attention to FP8 to see if that preserves negation tokens.
00:04:35 Tom: So hybrid FP8? That might be a good compromise if latency stays close.

00:05:00 Priya: We ran that hybrid quickly: p50 stayed ~155ms, p95 ~470ms, and the clinical negation regression dropped from 3% to 0.4% in our sample. Memory rose to 14.6GB though (vs 12.8). Throughput still +55% vs FP16.
00:05:25 Emma: That seems promising. For SageHealth the safety flows matter more than raw throughput.
00:05:31 Carlos: Agree. Also want to quantify hallucinations — any change?
00:05:36 Samir: We measured hallucination rate on the 1k labeled set: FP16 baseline 4.2%, INT8 4.5% (+0.3pp), FP8 5.1% (+0.9pp). Hybrid FP8 (FFN at FP16) 4.6% (+0.4pp). So the hybrid improves but still slightly worse than INT8.
00:06:00 Maya: Are those differences statistically significant? We need to justify any change for audit logs.
00:06:06 Priya: Some are within noise; we'll run a bootstrap with 10k bootstrap samples and push p-values to you. Expect clarity by Friday.

00:06:25 Jordan: Quick commercial note — for Dedicated pilot pricing we can include an experimental addendum that covers the hybrid FP8 profile validation with an SLA on regressions threshold. I'll draft the addendum.
00:06:36 Emma: Great. Also we'd like to surface metrics to our observability — token-level cost, latency by prompt type, and regression alerts. Can the Redwood console expose per-route regression counts?
00:06:46 Olivia: Yes, we can add a per-route metric and a regression alert hook based on your eval sets. We'll need the route names and sample prompt sets to wire it up.

00:07:10 Priya: Back to tech: we also tested continuous KV cache compatibility with INT8/FP8. No correctness issues there, but FP8 increased cache restore time by ~12ms due to dequant/decompress overhead on restore. Not huge but shows up on very low-latency flows.
00:07:33 Carlos: That 12ms might push some of our p50 SLOs for chat. If we go FP8 hybrid we need to validate chat latency.
00:07:42 Samir: Agreed. We'll run a chat-specific latency distribution next run.

00:08:00 Emma: Could we try per-layer mixed precision rules? For example keep embeddings and output head as FP16, attention at INT8 or FP8? What's feasible?
00:08:08 Priya: Yes — we shipped a rule engine to define per-layer dtype. It's somewhat manual for now, but we'll produce a recommended config that targets the regressions you flagged.
00:08:19 Tom: What's the ops-level determinism risk if we mix types?
00:08:23 Olivia: Minimal; the runtime keeps ops deterministic but the quantized kernels can have slight numerical reorderings. We'll add a determinism note for compliance as discussed.

00:09:05 Priya: Plan for next week: run three focused experiments — 1) hybrid FP8 with FFN in FP16 on the 5k set (full bootstrap in CI), 2) per-layer mixed precision targeting embeddings/output head preservation, 3) QAT sketch if we still see critical regressions. We'll attach the configs.
00:09:28 Emma: Good. For the canary do we need Dedicated or can we validate on Hosted?
00:09:33 Jordan: For latency and memory footprint dedicated is better; hosted has noise from multi-tenant but we can do an initial smoke test. For the canary you wanted a low-traffic Dedicated node — we'll provision 1x A100-style equivalent for two weeks.
00:09:51 Carlos: Cost estimate?
00:09:53 Jordan: I'll include pricing in the addendum but rough OPEX for two weeks on Dedicated pilot is in the addendum; we'll send that today.

00:10:20 Maya: On compliance we need audit logs for which quant profile served which request and a way to freeze the profile used for a date range. Can you do that?
00:10:28 Olivia: Yes, we can record profile IDs in the request trace and export that to your SIEM. We'll add the retention policy options in the docs we share.

00:11:00 Priya: Quick note on tooling — we added a delta mode to the eval harness that highlights token-level differences and flags negation/number/tokenization changes. Will upload sample output.
00:11:12 Samir: Also added a prompt-clustering pass; some regressions are concentrated in a cluster with long medical codes and lists. That will help prioritize QAT data.

00:11:40 Emma: On the sample where FP8 dropped "denies" can you reproduce locally with deterministic seed? I'd like to include in a risk doc.
00:11:47 Samir: Yes, Priya will create a repro harness and include the failing trace + logits.

00:12:10 Jordan: Perfect. Anything else from SageHealth before we recap?
00:12:15 Emma: One ask — can you include the throughput per-cost metric (tokens/sec per $) in the spreadsheet? We'll need to compare to our existing self-hosted infra numbers.
00:12:25 Jordan: Yes will add that.

00:12:40 Priya: Recap of technical outcomes: INT8 gives large mem and throughput wins with minimal metric drift; pure FP8 gives best perf but shows nontrivial regressions on sensitive prompts; hybrid FP8 (FFN in FP16) looks like the best compromise so far. Next steps: hybrid run + per-layer config + chat latency run.
00:13:03 Jordan: Commercial/ops recap: Jordan to send Dedicated pilot addendum + pricing, provision 1x node canary for two weeks; Redwood to expose regression alert hooks and per-route metrics in the Console.
00:13:18 Emma: Action items agreed. We'll aim to make a go/no-go decision for Dedicated pilot by 2026-10-15 after the hybrid results.

00:13:35 Jordan: Great, thanks everyone. We'll follow up with the updated spreadsheet and configs.
00:13:42 Olivia: I'll drop a short note for compliance and attach the determinism and audit logs doc.
00:13:48 End of call.
